tip.topic: AI and agents, including their derivatives (agent skills, plugins, frameworks, tooling, infrastructure).

depth.axis: Vertical: how deeply the project understands AI/agent principles (from 'just points to things' to 'explains the underlying mechanisms').

levels.very low: Does not explain anything. Pure resource list, link collection, awesome-list, name-only index, or a project whose description reveals no understanding of AI/agent internals.
levels.low: Explains only basic/introductory concepts. Answers 'what is it' at a surface level (e.g. beginner tutorials on basic AI ideas, glossary-level content).
levels.medium: Explains how to use it, not why it works. Project introductions, usage tutorials, API how-tos, application-level integration guides. Knows the interface, not the mechanism.
levels.high: Explains mechanisms and design rationale. Covers core algorithms, architecture design, engineering trade-offs, or how a system is built and why (e.g. agent orchestration design, retrieval pipeline internals).
levels.very high: Explains frontier/deep principles. Covers the latest AI architectures, advanced or complex agent principles, original research-level analysis, or rigorous derivation of why something works.

breadth.axis: Horizontal: how far the project is derived from the AI/agent core. Closer to the core = lower; more peripheral/adjacent = higher.

levels.very low: Is the AI/agent core itself: base models, core agent frameworks, core reasoning/planning mechanisms, the thing that defines AI/agent capability.
levels.low: Direct capability extensions of the core: agent skills, plugins, tools, prompt templates, memory modules, narrow capability add-ons tightly bound to agents.
levels.medium: Application-layer projects built on AI/agents: vertical apps, workflows, use-case integrations that use the core to solve a specific task.
levels.high: Supporting infrastructure for using AI/agents: environment setup, network/proxy configuration, deployment, gateways, SDK wrappers, runtime plumbing.
levels.very high: Peripheral or indirect: general dev tools or utilities only loosely related to AI/agents, or things that merely touch the ecosystem without serving it directly.

recency.axis: Determined by the item's release/publish time.

levels.very low: old/stale, not updated in a long time

tip.scoring_rule: Score depth and breadth independently using the level definitions above; do not let one influence the other. Example: an agent skill is breadth='low' regardless of how deep it is; a deep tutorial is depth='high'/'very high' regardless of how peripheral it is.
tip.filtering: Keep only items whose levels satisfy the required thresholds; reject any item below a required threshold. If a property cannot be judged from the description, exclude the item rather than guessing, unless a neutral default ('medium') is explicitly allowed.
tip.goal: Let the AI select and filter AI/agent projects using these four orthogonal properties and their levels.
